meta.title: Questions and answers
meta.description: Short answers about ADA certification, the exam, renewal, the registry and ADA training.

intro.title: Questions and answers
intro.lead: Short answers for candidates, certified doulas, families, insurers and agencies, and training providers.
intro.note: Fees and dates are on the program and exam pages.

cta.title: Write to ADA if your question is not answered here.

candidates.becomeA: Enroll in an ADA-approved training program and complete it. Then pass the ADA certification exam: a {written}-minute written exam and a {practical}-minute one-on-one practical exam. The pass mark is {pass}/{max}.
candidates.experienceQ: Do I need doula experience first?
candidates.experienceA: No. No prior doula experience is required. ADA-approved training programs are designed to take you from beginner to exam-ready.
candidates.costA: The ADA exam fee is {fee}. Training costs vary by program, and scholarships are available for qualified candidates.
candidates.scholarshipA: Yes. ADA offers need-based and merit-based scholarships to make doula training accessible. Scholarships cover partial or full training and exam fees.
candidates.languagesQ: Which languages are the training and the exam in?
candidates.languagesA: The training and the exam are available in {languages}. Say which language you prefer when you register for the exam.
candidates.trainingA: The intensive program runs {days} days and covers the {modules} modules of the ADA curriculum. Infant CPR from the American Red Cross is included.
candidates.registerQ: How do I register for the exam?
candidates.registerA: After you complete an ADA-approved training program, your training provider guides you through exam registration. You can also contact ADA directly at {email} or {phone}.
candidates.locationA: Exams are held at {location}. Additional exam locations may be available depending on demand. Contact ADA for the latest schedule.
candidates.resultsQ: When will I get my result?
candidates.resultsA: By email in about {days} business days. If you pass, ADA issues your certificate and your record appears in the ADA registry. If you do not pass, you can retake the exam after at least {wait} days. The retake fee is {retakeFee}.

doulas.validityQ: How long is ADA certification valid?
doulas.validityA: ADA certification is valid for {years, plural, one {# year} other {# years}}. After that, you renew it to stay certified.
doulas.renewA: Renewal costs {fee} and requires either professional reference letters or passing a recertification exam.
doulas.checkedQ: How do families and insurers check my certification?
doulas.checkedA: They search the ADA registry by certificate number, Doula ID or name. The record shows your status on the day they look.

families.checkQ: How do I check a doula’s certification?
families.checkA: Search the ADA registry by certificate number, Doula ID or name. It is free and needs no account. The record shows the doula’s status on the day you look.
families.findQ: How do I find an ADA-certified doula?
families.findA: Visit the Find a Doula page. You can also write to ADA at {email}.
families.insuranceQ: Does insurance cover an ADA-certified doula?
families.insuranceA: Insurers and benefit platforms that recognize ADA certification include {insurers}. Coverage depends on your plan, so contact your insurance provider for details.
families.concernQ: How do I report a concern about a doula?
families.concernA: Report it to ADA at {email}. Violations of the ADA Code of Conduct may result in disciplinary action, including suspension or revocation of ADA certification.

insurers.sourceQ: What is the primary source for an ADA credential?
insurers.sourceA: The live record in the ADA registry. A paper certificate shows status only on the day it was issued, so check the registry when you need the current status.
insurers.recognitionA: Insurers and benefit platforms that recognize ADA certification include {insurers}.
insurers.bulkQ: Can we check many doulas at once?
insurers.bulkA: Not on the website. Check each certificate number or Doula ID on Verify, or write to ADA at {email}.

providers.approvedQ: How does an organization become an Approved Training Provider?
providers.approvedA: Write to ADA at {email} and tell ADA about your organization and your program.
providers.registrationQ: Who registers our students for the exam?
providers.registrationA: After a student completes an ADA-approved training program, the training provider guides them through exam registration. Students can also contact ADA directly.
providers.curriculumQ: What does the ADA curriculum cover?

about.whatQ: What is the Asian Doula Alliance?
about.whatA: The Asian Doula Alliance (ADA) is a {taxCode} public charity dedicated to setting standards in postpartum care through culturally integrated training, certification and multilingual support. ADA is a dba of {legalName}, a California nonprofit public benefit corporation.
about.differentQ: How is ADA different from other doula certification organizations?
about.differentA: ADA bridges traditional Asian postpartum practices, such as zuo yuezi (sitting the month), herbal care and dietary customs, with modern evidence-based care. The ADA exam is available in {languages}, and insurers and benefit platforms including {insurers} recognize ADA certification.
about.onlyAsianQ: Is ADA only for Asian doulas?
about.onlyAsianA: No. ADA welcomes doulas of all backgrounds. ADA certification emphasizes cultural competency and multilingual skills, but any caregiver committed to culturally sensitive postpartum care can pursue it.
